text:
7. [RARC.5.6.8] Delivers the input's event and every derived event,
   internal and action alike, to the stream callback in the order they were
   processed ([RARC.5.8]).

   **Processed means propagated, per action.** Each RHS action's change to
   working memory is propagated through the network, truth-maintenance
   retractions included, before the change is recorded and before the next
   action of the same firing runs. A cascade retraction is therefore
   recorded ahead of the assert that caused it, and a firing that emits
   twice, where only the second emit invalidates a `no (...)`, records the
   retraction between its two asserts. Stream order is processing order,
   not causal order; a reader that takes precedence for causation
   attributes every cascade to the wrong cause.

   This is a rule's action. A host input is recorded on arrival, before
   what its evaluation produces ([RFCS.6.7]), and an engine withdrawal
   before the withdrawals it cascades into ([RFCS.7a.4], [LFST.7.3.6]).

idris.name: Rarc_5_6_8__event
idris.note: The two recorded events the cascade question turns on: a fact asserted by an action, and a fact retracted by truth maintenance because of one.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_8__cascade_is_per_action
idris.note: PROPAGATION IS PER ACTION. A firing emitting twice, where only the second invalidates a `no (...)`, interleaves the retraction BETWEEN the two asserts. This is 18_cascade_point's trace, and it is what tells the two apart: a single-emit firing cannot distinguish per-action from per-firing propagation, because both put the retract adjacent to the assert. Two emits separate them.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_8__cascade_precedes_its_cause
idris.note: PRECEDENCE IS NOT CAUSATION. The retraction an assert caused is recorded BEFORE that assert. What this rules out is the reading a consumer naturally brings to "in the order they were processed" -- that if X precedes Y in the stream, X did not come from Y. An operator log, a debugger and a replayer all read this clause; taking precedence for causation attributes every cascade to the wrong cause.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_8__is_not_per_firing
idris.note: The retraction does not wait for the firing's effects to finish. Stated as a mechanism rather than a trace deliberately: reordering a finished effect list would have matched the recorded bytes for a fraction of the work, and left two runtimes propagating against DIFFERENT working memories while agreeing on every observable the harness reads. A difference that can no longer be seen is worse than one that is pinned.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_8__record_action
idris.note: Propagate first, announce second: the clause's 'processed means propagated, per action'.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_8__record_firing
idris.note: Each action recorded in turn. This much the clause does settle -- the recorder emits in processing order and does not re-sort.
